item.title: Equitable funding for inclusive big team science
item.content:encoded:
Nature Human Behaviour, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41562-026-02638-7

Big team science seeks to make research more inclusive, but the cost of recruiting representative samples can vary markedly across countries. This risks reinforcing the very inequalities these collaborations seek to address. Pooling resources and asking funders to contribute according to their financial capacity could help to overcome these inequalities.

item.title: Causal role of human hippocampus in relational structure learning and inference
item.content:encoded:
Nature Human Behaviour, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41562-026-02627-w

Pan and colleagues show that the human hippocampus represents relational structures that support inference in changing environments and provide causal evidence that disrupting hippocampal activity impairs this ability.

item.title: Usage frequency predicts lexicalization across languages
item.content:encoded:
Nature Human Behaviour, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41562-026-02625-y

Why do almost all human languages have a word for ‘sun’, but fewer have a word for ‘weather’? Khishigsuren et al. find that the usefulness of a concept in communication predicts how often it appears in vocabularies across languages.
item.dc:title: Usage frequency predicts lexicalization across languages
